listings.title: From Near Obscurity to Iconic Works: Bach’s Cello Suites
listings.description: The six suites for unaccompanied cello by Johann Sebastian Bach—once dismissed as mere curiosities—are now revered as iconic works. They are performed worldwide by cellists of all ages, and they are moreover prominently used in pop culture such as film and television as well as in expressions of humanitarian advocacy. In this special Focus on the Humanities talk, Edward Klorman illustrates how and why Bach conceptualized this highly innovative music and tells the unlikely story of how the Cello

listings.title: SoundWaves: Origins - The Spark of Life
listings.description:
In the 2026-27 academic year, SoundWaves is exploring Origins - from the start of the universe to how we developed language, join us for this four-part series as we uncover the origins of who we are. As always, each lecture is paired with live, musical performance as it relates to the theme of the evening.

In this second part, we are diving into the Spark of Life as we celebrate the 50th edition of SoundWaves. Topics include geochemistry, microbiology, and astrobiology!

listings.title: Academy of St Martin in the Fields Chamber Ensemble
listings.description: The Academy of St Martin in the Fields Chamber Ensemble takes chamber music to the next level by harnessing the artistry of seasoned musicians who regularly perform together in one of the world’s finest orchestras. In this concert of all-string works, the group plays Mendelssohn’s Octet, the composer’s breakthrough masterpiece, with “a delirious sense of forward momentum” ( Washington Classical Review ), along with R. Strauss’s Sextet from Capriccio and more. Come hear an ensemble whose “signature balance of individuality and unity” ( The Arts Desk ) pairs virtuosity and elegance in equal measure. Program: Strauss: String Sextet from “Capriccio”  Erich Wolfgang Korngold: Sextet for Strings in D major, Op. 10 Mendelssohn: String Octet in E-flat major, Op. 20  View Program

listings.title: Terri Lyne Carrington + Social Science
listings.description: Grammy and Doris Duke Award winner, NEA Jazz Master, and founder of the Berklee College of Music’s Institute of Jazz and Gender Justice, Terri Lyne Carrington has centered activism throughout her four-decade career as a drummer, producer, and educator, and earned the admiration of Herbie Hancock, Dianne Reeves, and Esperanza Spalding along the way. With her ensemble, Social Science, Carrington enters her next era of “story-filled groove-music” (NPR’s Tiny Desk) that merges crafted instrumentals, soulful R&B vocals, and poetic rap into consciousness-raising songs in the lineage of The Last Poets and Gil Scott-Heron. Come out for inspiring music that puts today’s world into perspective. Terri Lyne Carrington, drums Matthew Stevens, guitar Christie Dashiell, vocals Simone Bridges, MC/DJ Oliver Unger, bass Ian Macklin-Simms, piano Santiago Bosch Ogly, keys

listings.title: WUD Film Committee Weekly Meeting
listings.description: UW-Madison students of all majors and levels of interest in film are welcome to join the WUD Film Committee—the only membership requirement is a love for movies.  WUD Film—a student-led team—hosts hundreds of diverse, innovative, and exciting movies for the University community.  Committee members help curate our film programming, manage our weekly screenings, and learn valuable leadership skills in the process.

listings.title: Exclusive film screening: "The New Gold Standard"
listings.description:
Interested in biomedical science? Cutting edge research techniques? Animal welfare?

Join us for an exclusive screening of "The New Gold Standard", a feature documentary by Steven Latham Productions. This film takes audiences inside some of the world’s leading research institutions to examine a scientific transformation already underway: the emergence of human-based research technologies that many scientists believe are reshaping how medicines are discovered, tested and approved.

listings.title: UW Cinematheque - Premieres
listings.description:
Cast: Anne-Laure Sellier
In the 1960s, an Italian Benedictine monk claimed to have invented a machine that allowed users to see into the past, as though on a TV set. While doing research, present-day academic Béatrice becomes fascinated by this “Chronovisor,” and plunges headlong into uncovering the truth about this mysterious device. This unusual and beguiling indie perfectly captures the sensation of going down a rabbit hole of dubious arcana.

listings.title: UW Cinematheque - New Restorations and Special Presentations
listings.description:
Cast: Gary Cooper, Clara Bow, Fredric March
A great burst of pre-code fun, Paramount on Parade was Paramount Pictures’ contribution to the all-star studio musical revue movie cycle of the early talkie years. Featuring 20 individual segments from 11 directors, the movie is literally a showcase for the incredible talents under contract: Gary Cooper, Clara Bow, Fredric March, Maurice Chavalier, Jean Arthur, Kay Francis, Jack Oakie, William Powell, Fay Wray, and lots, lots more stars.

listings.title: WUD Film Presents: The Matrix (1999) [Open Caption Screening]
listings.description:
USA | 140 min | R | Dir. The Wachowskis   "Neo believes that Morpheus, an elusive figure considered to be the most dangerous man alive, can answer his question -- What is the Matrix? Neo is contacted by Trinity, a beautiful stranger who leads him into an underworld where he meets Morpheus. They fight a brutal battle for their lives against a cadre of viciously intelligent secret agents. It is a truth that could cost Neo something more precious than his life." - Rotten Tomatoes   "The metaphorical properties of The Matrix are part of what makes it so seductive, along with the no-filler-all-killer action."-Peter Bradshaw of the Guardian

listings.description:
Cast: William Petersen, Brian Cox, Tom Noonan
Before Jonathan Demme’s The Silence of the Lambs, writer/director Michael Mann first brought Thomas Harris’ popular series of crime novels to the screen with this alluring adaptation of Red Dragon. Retreating to a quiet life with his family after taking down the infamous Hannibal Lecktor (Cox), FBI “manhunter” Will Graham (Petersen) returns to work following the emergence of an enigmatic new killer.

listings.description: Explore the world of music and rhythm! Each week, Tim leads children in singing and other musical activities that inspire creativity and connection. It’s an engaging experience for kids and families—free with admission.

listings.title: Li’l Music with Junko
listings.description:
Do you have a dancing baby? Discover Junko’s weekly music session where babies and toddlers can explore their natural love of rhythm. Together, you and your tiny dancer will bounce, sway, and rock with the music while learning simple rhythm patterns. They’ll build critical social skills over the weeks as they interact with new faces and watch the other babies in the room, and strengthen their bond with you through lap songs and movement activities.

It’s a wonderful way to get out of the house and connect with your baby or toddler through music and movement!

Leader Junko Yamauchi Stewart is a multitalented musician and educator, and founder of BENI Daiko Taiko Ensemble.

listings.description: Join MCM art educator Ms. Laurie for a weekly burst of color, texture, and joyful experimentation. Young children can freely explore art materials in a welcoming space designed especially for our youngest artists. It’s creativity without limits—or cleanup. Come make a beautiful mess with us! Free with general admission.

listings.title: Early Explorers Playgroup
listings.description: This playgroup is expertly designed for our earliest visitors. We will provide a space for infants and toddlers (2 years and under) and their caregivers to explore and play together, and engage in unstructured play that supports various aspects of child development. Parents and caregivers will have the opportunity to connect with one another over a variety of topics. Come meet other families and make new friends!

listings.title: Dairy Air
listings.description:
@

What’s in the air we breathe every day? Get ready to explore the science of breathing as we learn about Wisconsin air quality and how our lungs help keep us healthy through crafts, games, and interactive activities. Depending on the day’s activities, you might walk through giant lungs, spin a prize wheel, or enjoy a lively puppet show along the way. Come discover more with us!
 

“Sharing our Dairy Air” program is funded by Sanofi as part of The Air We Share initiative
